strategies.name: Sequential All-Reduce with Interleaved Scaling
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations with element-wise scaling and inverse-scaling between each stage, exactly as in the reference implementation. Total of 8 all-reduce dispatches with full vector payload (W*S elements each). Represents the baseline: maximal communication volume, no fusion, straightforward correctness.

strategies.name: Fused Scale-Reduce with Precomputed Coefficients
strategies.desc: Pre-computes the compound scaling factors across all 8 stages algebraically, then performs a single all-reduce on the pre-scaled input, followed by post-processing with the inverse compound factors. Reduces to 1 all-reduce dispatch but requires careful numerical stability handling and may increase local computation cost for the coefficient calculation.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Pipeline
strategies.desc: Converts each all-reduce into a reduce-scatter followed by all-gather pair, allowing intermediate local scaling operations to happen on smaller (S-sized) chunks rather than full (W*S) vectors. Results in 16 collective dispatches (2 per stage × 8 stages) but with smaller per-rank payloads and better memory locality for scaling operations.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Exploits the fact that only 4 distinct scaling factors exist (since a[r] depends on r%4) by grouping ranks into 4 cohorts and performing intra-cohort reductions first, then inter-cohort reductions with cohort-level scaling. Reduces redundant computation across ranks with identical scaling factors, requiring approximately 16-24 collective dispatches depending on topology but with smaller intermediate payloads.

strategies.name: Batched All-Reduce with Vectorized Buffers
strategies.desc:
Packs multiple stages' scaled buffers into a single larger tensor and issues fewer, larger all-reduce operations (e.g., 2-4 batched all-reduces covering multiple stages each), then unpacks and applies inverse scaling. Reduces dispatch overhead to 2-4 operations at the cost of increased memory footprint (2-4× staging buffer size) and more complex indexing logic.
